images.caption: Figure 2:An example of deep search in OpenDS-World.The example connects audiovisual identification, virtual-tour navigation, document inspection, and structured-data retrieval across multiple Web sources.

Figure 3:Three complementary properties of a real-world Web source.An Our World in Data page illustrates how a single source combines (A) diverse modalities, including text and visual charts; (B) heterogeneous formats, including HTML, CSV, JSON, and downloadable ZIP bundles; and (C) interactive access, including region selection, temporal indexing, and declarative API queries. Obtaining relevant evidence requires navigating these connected representations and source states.

Figure 5:Task diversity and statistics of OpenDS-World.Each annotated evidence-chain entry is characterized by its modality, resource format, and access type, collectively covering four modalities, 42 formats, and seven access types.
Top: representative Web sources illustrating these three dimensions.
Bottom: (a) modality coverage across 200 tasks, (b) format coverage across 200 tasks, and (c) task coverage of interactive access types. Access-type codes in (c) are defined in Table3.
Parentheses report counts; Other formats comprise 108 entries spanning 35 types.
Modality, format and access categories can overlap within a task.

Table 1:Main results on OpenDS-World.We evaluate frontier models across three difficulty levels which are defined by the number of correct human solvers out of the five participants assigned to each task: Low (≥2\geq 2; 54 tasks), Medium (11; 61 tasks), and High (00; 85 tasks). Evidence-attribute coverage within these difficulty groups is reported in Figure12(AppendixB.5).
For each level, we report accuracy (Acc, %),
total wall-clock time (/ h),
and total token consumption (Token / M.).
The shadedOverallcolumns summarize all 200 tasks.
Numbers in parentheses indicate correct answers. Bold accuracy values denote the best result in each group. The superscript(T)denotes text-only models.
